summary: Verified fix for Super Admin Platform Settings -> Login/Landing page background propagation. Backend API contract verified with pytest (4/4 pass). Frontend UI verified: /login page renders login_background_url from /api/platform/settings/public, LandingPage hero slideshow uses hero_backgrounds from same endpoint.

issues: Only offers 'Upload Background' file upload; there is no text input field for providing a URL. If the user's mental model is 'change the URL', they may not realize they must upload a file. Consider adding a URL text field as an alternative to file upload.

action_items: (Optional UX) Add a URL input alternative to file upload in Platform Settings > Login Background tab so Super Admins can paste external image URLs.
(Optional) Add data-testid to the platform settings tabs and inputs for easier automated testing.
critical_code_review_comments: LoginPage.js fetches platform settings on every mount. Consider caching in BrandingContext to avoid redundant calls.
Both LoginPage.js and LandingPage.js duplicate the default fallback URLs; consider extracting to a shared constants file.

The current stored login_background_url is a large base64 data URL (~300KB) - this bloats every /api/platform/settings/public response. Consider storing uploaded images as file URLs served from a CDN/static route instead.
seed_data_creation: None - test creates, verifies, and restores original platform settings
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend test file at /app/backend/tests/test_platform_settings.py covers public settings GET, authenticated GET, and PUT with persistence verification. Login background is currently stored as a base64 data URL from a prior file upload. Fix verified: LoginPage and LandingPage now correctly fetch and use /api/platform/settings/public.
rca of the issue: The original bug was that LoginPage.js and LandingPage.js used hardcoded default background URLs regardless of what Super Admin saved in Platform Settings. Fix applied: both components now fetch settings from /api/platform/settings/public on mount (when in non-subdomain context) and use those values with hardcoded URLs only as fallback. Verified via visual inspection that /login now displays the map image stored as login_background_url in DB (was displaying the previous default before the fix).
